verses.text: So, here’s Jesus the Messiah’s family story: David’s descendant, Abraham’s descendant. The roots go way back, fam. 🌱
Abraham’s line went to Isaac, Isaac’s to Jacob, and Jacob’s to Judah and his brothers. The family tree keeps branching.
Judah and Tamar had Perez and Zerah. Perez’s line carried on through Hezron to Ram—generation handoff, no gaps.
Ram’s line went through Amminadab and Nahshon to Salmon. One name passes the story to the next.
Salmon and Rahab had Boaz; Boaz and Ruth had Obed; Obed became Jesse’s dad. This family line is still growing. 🌿
Jesse became father to King David. David became Solomon’s father through Uriah’s wife—yes, that story is part of the family record too.
Solomon’s line went through Rehoboam and Abijah to Asa. The royal family story rolls on.
Asa’s line went through Jehoshaphat and Joram to Uzziah. One generation passing the baton to the next.
Uzziah became Jotham’s father, Jotham Ahaz’s, and Ahaz Hezekiah’s. The names keep coming, fam.
Hezekiah became Manasseh’s father, Manasseh Amon’s, and Amon Josiah’s. The line keeps moving.
Josiah became father to Jechoniah and his brothers around the time the people were taken away to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became Shealtiel’s father, and Shealtiel became Zerubbabel’s. The family story picks up again.
Zerubbabel’s line went through Abiud and Eliakim to Azor. Generation after generation, still rolling.
Azor became Zadok’s father, Zadok Achim’s, and Achim Eliud’s. The family record keeps its pace.
Eliud became Eleazar’s father, Eleazar Matthan’s, and Matthan Jacob’s. Another handoff in the line.
Jacob became Joseph’s father. Joseph was Mary’s husband, and Mary gave birth to Jesus, the one called the Messiah.
Count the generations: fourteen from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the Babylon exile, and fourteen from that exile to the Messiah. The pattern’s locked in.
Here’s how Jesus the Messiah was born: Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was righteous. He didn’t want to shame her in public, so he planned to end the engagement quietly.

While Joseph was thinking it over, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child she’s carrying is from the Holy Spirit.”
“She’ll give birth to a son. Name him Jesus, because he’ll save his people from their sins.”
All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet. The promise was coming through, just as written:
“Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son. They’ll call him Immanuel”—meaning “God with us.” ✨
Joseph woke up and did what the Lord’s angel told him. He took Mary as his wife.
But he didn’t have sexual relations with her before she gave birth to her firstborn son. Joseph named him Jesus.
